If there is no record of what was there at the start, everything counts as already there and only yt-dlp's leftovers go.

- PlaybackController offers Player.audioDevices and Player.audioDevice to QML, plus Player.setAudioDevice(name). The choice and the device's name are saved as the settings player.audio_device and player.audio_device_name.

- New `--audio-devices [videoId]` diagnostic: it lists what mpv sees and what the menu offers. Given a song, it switches through every device while the song plays and reads the play position after each switch.

U02, scrolling — what I measured
I added `--scroll-test` (src/scrollselftest.cpp). It scrolls the open page by sending timestamped wheel events and reads frame times and how long the interface's thread was held up. The machine uses Direct3D 11 on the Parallels adapter, 120 Hz, 2x scaling, and Windows is set to 6 lines per notch.

Qt's own wheel handling was the cause. It turns every wheel event into a new fling with a speed floor and ignores how far the wheel turned, so nothing moved faster than about 600 px/s. Release behaved the same as Debug (the Qt libraries are the same release DLLs in both builds).

Frame times while scrolling were already fine (8.3 ms median). The other real cost was cover decoding on the interface's thread: 10–35 ms each, one of 190 ms. On Home, 22 covers took 213 ms.

Before and after, 100-song playlist page (Debug; Release figures were the same):

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| One notch | 144 px, still after 266 ms | 200 px, still after 115–122 ms |
| Five quick notches | 424 px (85 per notch), 461 ms | 1000 px, 223–269 ms |
| Touchpad-style swipe, 8 notches' worth in small events | 161–190 px | 1600 px |
| Slow touchpad drag, 2.5 notches' worth | 105 px | 500 px |
| Wheel from top to bottom | 32 notches at 115 px, 3.8 s | 19 notches at 194 px, 2.2 s |

- Hover cost: with the pointer over a long list, the glide's frames were 13–25 ms at the median, against 8.3 ms with the pointer off the window (`--scroll-away`). The cost is rows passing under the pointer lighting up. Holding hover still while the wheel moves the page brought the median back to 8.2–8.4 ms, 95th percentile about 10 ms (Debug and Release).
- Covers: after the change, none are decoded on the interface's thread. Home's worst hold-up while loading fell from 120–202 ms to 78 ms (Release).

U02, scrolling — what changed
- New `ScrollPage` component, used by all ten views.
- New `SmoothWheel` wheel handler, used by ScrollPage, the queue list and the sidebar list:
  - one notch = the system's lines per notch × 100/3 px, which is what browsers use, eased over 120 ms (Theme.quick);
  - notches that arrive during a glide add to where it's going;
  - touchpad steps smaller than a notch, and trackpad pixel movements, are applied immediately;
  - if anything else moves the page mid-glide (a drag, the scroll bar, a new page), the glide stops.
- While the wheel is moving the page, ScrollPage holds hover still and keeps the pointer's current shape. It uses a new `Chrome.cursorShape()` helper for that.
- ArtworkFetcher now decodes covers on its own small thread pool, and the finished picture is handed back on the main thread.
- DESIGN.md explains the wheel behaviour and records the new use of Theme.quick. README.md documents both new flags and drops the "device button unwired" known gap.

A song the listener explicitly queued therefore goes into the queue marked as an autoplay song.
findings.scenario: Autoplay adds song R and it starts playing. The listener opens the player bar's dots and chooses Add to queue, then adds song D from a track list. addToQueue puts R's copy at the first radio row, flagged fromRadio, so it becomes radioStartIndex. The AUTOPLAY heading moves above it, and D is inserted before it, so the queue order no longer matches the order things were queued. When the copy plays, openPlayEvent records source "radio" and Last.fm is told it was not chosen by the user. A later "Don't suggest <artist>" runs pruneRadio, which silently removes it. Play next does the same: the copy lands straight after the current song and pulls the AUTOPLAY heading above everything queued after it.

With fewer shelves after the rebuild, Forward to recs:6 shows the old list unchanged.
findings.fix: Put something stable in the view name, for example the shelf title or kind plus seed ("recs:<generation>:<index>", or the title). In openMore, match the shelf by that key rather than by index. When the shelf no longer exists, say so rather than reusing m_more.

findings.problem: F18 makes the main download button cancel while the download is "processing", when FFmpeg is converting or tagging. YtDlpRequest::cancel (ytdlp.cpp 239-246) calls QProcess::kill on yt-dlp only. Its FFmpeg child keeps running and holds the input and output files open. removeLeftovers runs straight away, QFile::remove fails on the locked files (Windows sharing violation), and FFmpeg then finishes writing. This goes against the menu's "nothing is left behind".
findings.scenario: On Windows, click the three-dots (processing) button to cancel a download into Music\Monolist. The row disappears and the song reads as not downloaded, but "Artist - Title [id].webm" and the converted "… [id].mp3" stay in the folder untracked by the database. Downloading it again records the leftover .mp3, which yt-dlp takes as already downloaded. The .webm is now in m_before as "already there" and is never cleaned up. This was already reachable from TrackMenu's Cancel download before this batch; F18 puts it on the main button.
findings.fix: Kill the whole process tree on cancel: a Windows job object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, or taskkill /T under Q_OS_WIN, and a process group with kill(-pgid) on POSIX. Or, in the processing state, wait for the process to exit before calling removeLeftovers. Otherwise keep processing non-cancellable as before.

findings.problem: The mini video panel (324x184 logical, 24 px above the player bar) floats over the page, but no page leaves room for it. Page content ends 96 px above the bar (bottomPadding 96), so the last two or three rows of any list sit under the panel and cannot be scrolled out from under it. Their heart, download, length and ••• controls cannot be reached.
findings.scenario: Seen in the running app (ui3/mini-pl.png). Open the Night Drive playlist, 7 rows, and play LrM_Y39Gmhk with the video on and Now Playing closed. The panel covers rows 5–7 from the album column rightwards, and the page cannot scroll. Clicking where row 6's download button should be opens Now Playing instead. It is the same at the end of a long playlist that has been scrolled all the way down.

findings.problem: While a row is dragged, the red drop rule always crosses the carried row and is drawn on top of it (header z:3 against the held row's z:2). The row is carried from its middle, and the gap is the row boundary nearest the pointer, so the rule is always within ±half a row of the row's centre. It reads as a red strikethrough through the dragged song's title and artist rather than as a gap between rows. QueuePanel.qml:154/156 does the same (rule z:3, held row z:2).
findings.scenario: Seen in ui3/drag-mid.png. In a playlist, drag Sky by its grip down between EVIL J0RDAN and Location. A 2 px red line runs through 'Sky · Playboi Carti · Whole Lotta Red · 3:14' inside the paper plate, and the rows it passes are half-hidden above and below it. In the queue (ui3/q-compare2.png) the rule sits on the plate's own border.
findings.fix: Put the rule where the plate is not. Either open a real gap (move the rows below the drop point down one row height, a position change that DESIGN 2.3 allows) and put the rule there, or draw the plate over the rule and offset the plate so the gap stays visible.

findings.problem: Pressing the grip calls forceActiveFocus on the row, and nothing a mouse user does afterwards takes the focus away. After an ordinary mouse drag, the moved row keeps the red 2 px focus rule on its left edge, and the grip replaces its number. Clicking the page's empty area does not clear it. It only goes after Esc or after leaving the page. QueuePanel.qml:297 behaves the same way. The red mark competes with the playing row's red, which DESIGN reserves for what is active.
findings.scenario: Seen in ui3/focus-compare.png. Drag 'Playboy' to row 5, then click empty space on the page. Row 5 still shows the red left rule and the grip instead of '5'. Navigating Home and back clears it.
findings.fix: Give the row keyboard focus only when a key is used (for example, take focus on the grip's first Alt+arrow or Menu key), or drop focus on release when the drag moved the row. Alternatively, show the focus mark only for visualFocus-style keyboard focus.

findings.problem: The narrow Now Playing video switch mixes two conventions. It shows the 'image' glyph while the picture plays (the PlateButton convention: the glyph is what a click gives you), and it also colours that glyph red while the video is wanted (the IconButton convention: red means the thing it controls is on). A red 'image' glyph reads as 'the cover is on'. The player bar's switch on the same screen shows a red 'video' glyph for the same state.
findings.scenario: Seen in ui3/np-narrow.png, a 900 px-wide window with Now Playing open and a video playing. The switch at the end of the song line is a red picture icon, while the bar below shows a red camera icon for the same switch.
findings.fix: On paper, follow the bar: iconName 'video' (or dots while waiting), red when on, grey when off. Keep 'image' only on the plate version that sits on the picture.

findings.problem: The player bar's new ••• button is dimmed with nothing loaded (enabled: hasSong, opacity 0.4) but keeps hoverEnabled true. Qt 6.11 still reports a disabled Button as hovered, so its glyph turns ink under the pointer. This is exactly what F19 fixed for the heart beside it (LikeButton hoverEnabled: enabled) and for the new video button (line 362), but not for this button.
findings.scenario: Seen in ui3/empty-zoom.png. Start with an empty MONOLIST_DATA_DIR so no song is loaded, then hover the bar's dots. They darken from light grey to near-ink, while the dimmed heart next to them stays grey. The click does nothing.
findings.fix: Add hoverEnabled: enabled to that IconButton, or better, set hoverEnabled: enabled in IconButton.qml itself so every disabled IconButton (the shelf arrows too) stops answering the pointer.

findings.problem: 'Not interested' and 'Don't suggest <artist>' appear for every queue row and for the playing song. The menu's own comment says they make no sense for songs the listener chose, yet QueueModel exposes a fromRadio role that could tell autoplay's songs from chosen ones. findings.scenario: Seen in ui3/q-menu-crop.png. Use Night Drive → Add all to queue, then right-click 'Playboy' in the queue. The menu ends with 'Not interested' and 'Don't suggest HUGEL & Malachiii'. The playing song's menu from the player bar offers 'Don't suggest Playboi Carti' for a song from the user's own playlist. findings.problem: A playlist search shows the same label twice, about 70 px apart, with different meanings. findings.problem: SectionHeader's title has no width limit and no elide, but this batch places it with an action link and a long, changing title: RecsView uses the shelf title with PLAY ALL, ShelfView uses the listing title with PLAY ALL, and ArtistView uses the songs title with SHOW ALL. reviews.checked: Read the whole diff 1d9b6e7..HEAD for the data paths. Migrations: the is_video ALTERs on tracks, recent, playlist_tracks and downloads, plus artist_links in createSchema. These run before any reader on both a fresh database and an existing one, and every reader and writer uses the matching column indexes (readSongs, reloadRecent, TrackModel, DownloadLibraryModel). Writes never clear the video flag: MAX() in the ON CONFLICT/UPDATE clauses of recordHistory, storeLike, recordStored and the tracks update. Playlist order: movePlaylistEntry renumbers inside one transaction, every reader orders by position, id, and the model moves in place only when it matches the database. Not-interested: persisted in play_events, loadTurnedDown reads it all back at construction (not limited to the 4000-event window), undo deletes by id, closePlayEvent updates by stored id so turn-downs cannot hit the wrong row, and the taste profile skips notInterestedArtist. The output device is persisted in settings, restored after setLibrary, and applied once mpv lists its devices. SQL threads: ArtistLinks::remember hands work to its own thread, and the recommender reads the database only on the main thread; the pool in ArtworkFetcher does no SQL. Lifetimes: destruction order in main.cpp for ArtistLinks, the hook guard, Recommender/radio filter, ArtworkFetcher and VideoSurface (render context freed by the last surface before MpvEngine goes). ArtworkResponse finishes after cancel, as QML expects. InnerTube send, slot and generation handling. Catalog page, listing, artist, collection and mix stale-answer checks; MediaExtractor card-search generation and cancel when switching chips. QueueModel::move keeps the current row, the radio flag and the original order correct. Downloads: chooseDirectory priority, the self-test's env save/restore and its no-mkpath check, removeLeftovers against the before-snapshot, and every --download/test guard. Nothing was built or run; all findings come from reading the code.

findings.problem: On an album or playlist page, "Download all" calls Downloads.enqueue without the isVideo argument, so it defaults to false. recordStored only falls back to what `recent`, `playlist_tracks` or `tracks` already know about the id, and a YouTube Music playlist page is usually made of songs the app has never stored. So P03's claim that downloads keep the video flag does not hold for this path. PlaylistView.qml:87 has the same omission, but the playlist_tracks fallback covers it there.
findings.scenario: Open an artist page, press SHOW ALL on its Videos shelf (it opens as a playlist page), and press Download all. Every downloads row is written with is_video=0, and so is the new tracks row. Play the videos later from Downloads, or from Songs after a restart: no picture is offered, even though downloading the same rows one by one through each row's DownloadButton, which passes row.isVideo, would have kept the flag.
findings.fix: Pass `track.isVideo === true` as the sixth argument in PageView.downloadAll, and do the same in PlaylistView for consistency.

findings.problem: L02 added "Save to library" to album cards, and it hands the raw card to Library.setSaved. Album cards never set `artist` (parseCard fills card.artist only for watch-endpoint cards), so setSaved falls back to parsing the subtitle. The cards on an artist page and in its Albums/Singles SHOW ALL grid read "Album • 2019" or just "2019". The only part after the kind is a year, which is skipped, so the saved album is stored with artist '' permanently. Saving from the album's own page uses Catalog.page, which has the header artist, so it was never affected.
findings.scenario: Open Radiohead's artist page, open the dots menu on an album in the Albums shelf, and choose Save to library. The `albums` row is written with artist = ''. From then on the Library's saved-album card shows no artist, and nothing ever fills it in.
findings.fix: Give the card its artist before saving. For example, ArtistView/ShelfView can add `artist: root.name` (or the listing kicker) to the cards they hand to Menus.openCard. Alternatively, when the card lacks an artist, CardMenu can save through a page lookup instead.

findings.problem: The --download guard accepts MONOLIST_DOWNLOAD_DIR alone. That variable only moves the folder, not the database, so AppDatabase still opens the user's real library. recordStored then writes a `downloads` row and a `tracks` row into it, both pointing into the scratch folder. The README and the brief present "one of those two" as the safe way to test.
findings.scenario: `$env:MONOLIST_DOWNLOAD_DIR='C:\...\scratch\dl'; monolist --download LrM_Y39Gmhk`, with MONOLIST_DATA_DIR unset. The test song becomes a permanent row in the user's real Songs library and Downloads table. Once the scratch folder is cleaned up, the downloads row is hidden (loadStored skips missing files), but the tracks row stays in the library, pointing at a file that no longer exists.
findings.fix: Make --download require MONOLIST_DATA_DIR, as --download-cleanup-test does; MONOLIST_DOWNLOAD_DIR can still choose the folder on top of it. Update the README line to match.

findings.problem: Cancelling while a download is "processing" (now also possible from every DownloadButton, via F18) kills only yt-dlp: YtDlpRequest::cancel -> QProcess::kill. FFmpeg, yt-dlp's child, keeps running. fail() then calls removePartialFiles straight away. On Windows the source stream and FFmpeg's output are still open without FILE_SHARE_DELETE, so the QFile::remove calls in removeLeftovers (line 622) fail silently. FFmpeg then finishes writing its output. F13's promise that the cleanup removes "FFmpeg's cut-off output" does not hold here: both files stay in <Music>/Monolist with no database row. On the next attempt they are in m_before, so they count as "already there" and are never cleaned up.
findings.scenario: On Windows, with the format set to MP3, download a song and click the button while it shows "Finishing up. Click to cancel". Afterwards <Music>/Monolist holds "Artist - Title [id].webm" and a complete, untagged "Artist - Title [id].mp3". The Downloads page lists neither, and retrying the download does not remove them.
findings.fix: Kill the whole process tree on cancel: on Windows, a job object or `taskkill /T /PID`; on Unix, a process group. Alternatively, when the request was cancelled in the Processing state, wait for FFmpeg to exit and run removeLeftovers afterwards, or retry the removal once the files are released.

findings.problem: openPage drops a stale answer only by `browseId != m_pageId`. Opening page A, then B, then A again while A's first browse is still in flight (possible on a slow link, because Back re-calls openPage through openCurrentPage) leaves two A answers that both pass the check. Whichever lands second resets m_pageTracks, m_pageFeed and m_pageNext, but keeps m_pageKeys and m_pageRequestOut. There are two bad outcomes. (a) If a part has already landed in between, keys 101-200 are in the set, the list is reset to 100 rows with the first token, and the next fetch sees nothing new and clears m_pageNext for good, so the playlist ends at 100. (b) If a part is in flight and the second answer's token differs, fetchPagePart's callback returns at line 341 without clearing m_pageRequestOut. pageLoadingMore then stays true and Play, Shuffle and Download all keep waiting forever. openListing has the same key-only check.
findings.scenario: On a slow connection, open a 700-song playlist A from Home, click another album card B before A appears, and press Back. A's first answer lands, and you scroll so the second hundred loads. A's second answer then lands: the page shows 100 songs, and scrolling or Play never gets past them. If A's second answer lands while that part is still in flight instead, "Loading more songs…" never ends.
findings.fix: Stamp every openPage and openListing with a generation counter, as playCollection and loadArtistMix already do, and drop answers from older generations. In fetchPagePart, clear m_pageRequestOut (or check the generation) before returning on a stale token.

reviews.checked:
Read AGENT_BRIEF and the full diff 1d9b6e7..HEAD, one file at a time. Focused on artworkcache.cpp/.h (moving cover decoding to a thread pool: response lifetime, cancel, shutdown), SmoothWheel.qml, ScrollPage.qml and scrollselftest.cpp (U02: wheel maths, the pixel/touchpad path, hover hold, Chrome.cursorShape, macOS/Linux event shapes), windowchrome.cpp (the new code sits inside Q_OS_WIN), videosurface.cpp (the shared render context, vid=no after 400 ms, the software render in updatePaintNode), mpvengine.cpp and the stub (async audio-device), catalog.cpp together with PageView, ShelfView, CardGrid and TrackTable (continuation, feeding rows, resets), mediaextractor append and move, library.cpp (movePlaylistEntry, reloadPlaylistSongs, addAllToPlaylist is in a transaction and the index exists), recommender.cpp (fingerprint queries on every refresh, the owned set, turn-downs), artistlinks.cpp (in memory, saves batched), downloadmanager.cpp (filesFor and removeLeftovers listings; the folder is local on this VM, so not reported), playbackcontroller.cpp, streamresolver.cpp and ytdlp.cpp (muxed tier), QueuePanel and RecRow/RecsView (RecsView appends properly), and Main.qml's full-screen handling.

Portability: grepped every new or changed source for WinAPI, Q_OS_ guards, .exe, C++20-only constructs (none found) and std:: usage against standard includes (fine; the project is C++17). Checked the self-test headers' forward declarations and the new QML APIs (FrameAnimation, HoverHandler.blocking, Application.styleHints all need Qt 6.5 or later).

Ran the already-built Debug and Release exes against a scratch MONOLIST_DATA_DIR (agentdata\perfreview), using network API calls only and no downloads: `--search --filter playlists` to find long playlists, and `--view page:<id> --page <id> --all` on a 62-song, a 111-song and a 305-song playlist. The 305-song one gave 25-row batches of up to 123 ms in Debug and 175 ms in Release; the Release run came out slower than Debug here, which suggests normal variance rather than a real difference. Did not run --scroll-test, because it moves the real pointer, and did not drive full-screen video or any download.

Considered and dropped:
- A wrong direction with Windows' 'one screen at a time' wheel setting: Qt maps WHEEL_PAGESCROLL to 3.
- macOS mouse-wheel pixel deltas: they are applied at once, which is close to native.
- The download-folder listing on each download start: small on the local Music folder here.
- The recommender's owned-set computation on the GUI thread: minor.

findings.problem: A03 lets a playlist page grow to 5,000 rows (catalog.cpp:15, kPageSongCap), but the song table is still a Column plus Repeater, so every row gets a full delegate. Each row is about 35 items: roughly eight QtQuick.Shapes icons (the grip, three inside LikeButton, three in DownloadGlyph, the dots button), each parsing SVG paths when created, plus two ArtistLines (a Text, a Rectangle, a MouseArea, two HoverHandlers and FontMetrics each), three Buttons and about ten handlers. Every view is always instantiated (Main.qml ViewFade), so the rows stay alive after the user navigates away. Play, Shuffle, Add all to queue, Add all to playlist and Download all go through withWholePage and wait until Catalog.pageLoadingMore is false. That flag stays true until m_pageFeed is empty (catalog.cpp:296), which means waiting until every row delegate has been built, not just until the data has arrived.
findings.scenario: Measured here with `--view page:VLPLXCoHsJ9oLec7aYGojOIj3Acu7wMKjADm --page VLPLXCoHsJ9oLec7aYGojOIj3Acu7wMKjADm --all` (305 songs): each 25-row batch took up to 88–123 ms in Debug and 170–175 ms in Release. A 5,000-song playlist is 200 such batches. Pressing Play therefore means about 20–35 s of 6–10 fps interface with the button showing dots before anything plays. After that, about 175k items including about 40k Shapes stay resident until another page opens, and opening another page then tears them all down at once (the model reset in openPage). PlaylistView and Liked songs use the same Repeater, and 'Add all to playlist' can now put thousands of rows into them.
findings.fix: Virtualise the table: make PageView (and PlaylistView) a ListView with the header as `header:` and the rows as delegates, instead of a Repeater inside a Column. Separately, run the whole-playlist actions as soon as every part has arrived (m_pageRequestOut false and m_pageNext empty), using pageTrackList() plus m_pageFeed, rather than after the table is built. Also make rows lighter: create the LikeButton, DownloadButton and grip Icon lazily, for example with a Loader on hover or when a row is liked or downloaded.

findings.problem: Every row of every TrackTable carries a DownloadButton, even when showDownloads is false (it is only hidden, and its bindings still run), and all views exist at the same time. Its downloadState and progress bindings depend on the global Downloads.revision. DownloadManager::touch() fires on every enqueue (downloadmanager.cpp:210) and on every whole-percent progress step. PageView.downloadAll (views/PageView.qml:78) calls Downloads.enqueue once per track in a JS loop, so each enqueue synchronously re-evaluates two bindings, each calling into C++ (stateFor or progressFor), for every row in the app. That is O(N²), and A03 now allows N up to 5,000. Library.revision works the same way: `liked` calls isLiked for every row, and the new reloadPlaylistSongs() touches it on every add to or removal from a playlist.
findings.scenario: Open a 1,000-song playlist and press Download all. After the rest of the page loads, 1,000 enqueues each re-evaluate at least 2,000 row bindings: about 2M JS-to-C++ calls inside one JS loop, so the window stops responding for seconds. At 5,000 rows it is about 50M calls, which is minutes. While the downloads then run, each percent step of each concurrent download re-evaluates 10,000 bindings for the 5,000-row page that stays alive in the hidden PageView.
findings.fix: Add Downloads.enqueueAll(list) that touches once. Replace the global revision with notifications for one video at a time, for example a stateChanged(videoId) signal the button filters on, or state and progress as model roles updated with dataChanged on the affected row. Do the same for Library.revision and isLiked.

findings.problem: FullscreenVideo (U03) sizes the VideoSurface to fill the screen at the picture's aspect ratio. updatePaintNode then asks mpv's software renderer to draw each frame at the item's size in device pixels, and it does so during the scene-graph sync, while the GUI thread is blocked. It then creates a brand-new texture from that QImage for every frame. The source is usually far smaller than the screen: itag 18 is 640×360, and the video tier is capped by the height setting. So the CPU upscales every frame to screen resolution before the GPU ever sees it.
findings.scenario: A 16:9 video in full screen on a 14-inch MacBook Pro (1512×982 pt at 2x): every frame is software-scaled to 3024×1701 (5.1 Mpx, about 20 MB of BGR0) while the GUI thread waits, then about 20 MB is uploaded. At 30 fps that is about 600 MB/s of scaling and upload, plus tens of milliseconds per frame of blocked GUI thread. The strip and player bar over the picture become sluggish and frames drop. A 5K display is 14.7 Mpx per frame. Not measured here, because triggering full screen needs the real keyboard; reasoned from the code.
findings.fix: Render at the smaller of the item size and the video's own size (g_engine->videoSize(), which is dwidth/dheight), and let the QSGSimpleTextureNode scale it on the GPU (Linear filtering is already set). Better still, move mpv_render_context_render out of the sync phase: render into a double buffer from the frame callback on a worker, and only swap and upload in updatePaintNode.

findings.problem: When a 'show all' listing loads another part, Catalog::fetchListingPart rebuilds the whole `sections` QVariantList and emits listingChanged (catalog.cpp:494). ShelfView's Repeater is bound to a JS array taken from Catalog.listing, so every part resets the model: every section Column, CardGrid and ShelfCard is destroyed and created again (each card has an Artwork with a MultiEffect). Every cover is then requested again, and QQuickPixmapCache's cache of images no longer in use is only about 2 MB.
findings.scenario: SHOW ALL on a shelf whose grid continues, such as a long discography or new releases. Each time the reader nears the end, part N arrives and all cards from parts 1 to N are rebuilt, which is O(N²) work over the scroll. Every cover on screen falls back to its placeholder until it has been fetched from the disk cache and decoded again. The author notes that grid continuations were never seen live, so this may be rare, but the code path resets whenever it runs.
findings.fix: Expose the listing's cards as a model that is appended to with beginInsertRows, as pageTracks is. Alternatively, keep a ListModel in QML and append to it from a listingAppended(cards) signal, as RecsView already does with moreAppended.

findings.problem: enterVideoFullscreen records window.visibility, and leaveVideoFullscreen restores with showMaximized() or showNormal(). A window that was already FullScreen before the video took over is not handled: that can be macOS native full screen from the green traffic light, which this app keeps, or a Linux window manager's full screen. Such a window is dropped to Normal on exit.
findings.scenario: On macOS, the user has Monolist in its own full-screen Space and presses F to fill it with the video. On Esc, F, a double-click or the strip's button, showNormal() pulls the whole app out of its full-screen Space, which is not what the user left it in.
findings.fix: If visibilityBeforeFullscreen === Window.FullScreen, skip showFullScreen() on entry and leave the window state alone on exit, only removing the video overlay.

findings.problem: movePlaylistEntry reads every entry of the playlist and UPDATEs the position of every row, for each single move, synchronously on the GUI thread. It then rebuilds the cover mosaic (artworksFor) and reloads the whole playlists model. One step therefore costs O(playlist size), even though only the rows between `from` and `to` change.
findings.scenario: A 5,000-song playlist of the user's own, which Add all to playlist from a long page (A03) now makes easy. The user grabs a row and holds Alt+Down: key repeat sends about 30 moves a second, each rewriting 5,000 rows plus the (playlist_id, position) index and reloading m_playlists, so the interface falls behind the key repeat. Each dropped drag pays the same cost.
findings.fix: Read (id, position) together and UPDATE only the rows whose stored position differs from their new index, so a one-step move writes two rows. Renumber the whole playlist only when the positions turn out to be repeated or have gaps.

findings.problem: This batch added MpvEngine::setVideoWatched (declared at mpvengine.h:73 and called from videosurface.cpp) but did not define it in the MONOLIST_NO_MPV stub, even though the summary says the build without libmpv got a stub. That configuration was already not compiling before this batch: the stub defines load(QString, bool), which does not match the header's five-argument load, and videosurface.cpp is always listed in the qt_add_qml_module SOURCES and includes <mpv/render.h>. It is now broken in one more way.
findings.scenario: Configure with -DMONOLIST_NO_MPV=ON, for example for a first build on a Mac without libmpv, which is what the option is for. The build fails to compile on the stub's load(), then fails to link on setVideoWatched and on videosurface.cpp's mpv_render_* calls.
findings.fix: Add setVideoWatched and the five-argument load to the stub, and leave videosurface.cpp out (or give it a stub) when MONOLIST_NO_MPV is on. Alternatively, drop the option.

outcomes.finding: Recs See all history keyed only by shelf index
outcomes.why: Confirmed. The view key is now Recs.moreKey(shelf) = generation:index:kind|title. openMore(key) keeps the open list when the key matches. outcomes.finding: DownloadButton cancel while processing leaves FFmpeg running and files locked
outcomes.why: Confirmed from the code: QProcess::kill ends yt-dlp only. YtDlpRequest now puts yt-dlp in a job object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE on Windows, or its own process group via setpgid on POSIX. The new stopProcess() ends the whole tree (TerminateJobObject, then waits for ActiveProcesses to reach 0 for up to 2 s; kill(-pgid) on POSIX) before settleFailed runs the cleanup. Builds and passes --download-cleanup-test. Not exercised against a live FFmpeg cancel, which needs a real download.

In the queue a row steps to its neighbour's row slot, so captions stay put. Verified with real mouse drags in both a playlist and the queue.

outcomes.finding: TrackTable is not virtualised; whole-page actions wait for every row

outcomes.finding: DownloadButton/TrackMenu bindings on global Downloads.revision: O(N^2) Download all
outcomes.why: Confirmed. enqueueAll updates the rows once for the whole list. Percentage steps now bump a separate progressRevision, which only buttons whose state is 'downloading' read. revision moves only on state changes, and pump() bumps it when downloads start. The Library.revision part was not changed: it moves once per user action (O(rows)), not in a loop.
